To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) emotional body language displayed in an animated character is perceived similarly by observers to that displayed by an actor; (2) however the videos of the actors were found to be significantly more believable and natural than the animated character, whilst displaying the exact same emotional body language; (3) there is no difference in the perception of positive emotions displayed by an actor and an animated character, whilst the animated character is found less believable and natural than an actor when displaying negative emotions.
animated body language is interpreted similarly to real actors.
animated body language is an appropriate way to communicate emotion, however, there is a difference in the perception of emotional body language between animated characters and real actors.

the use of Virtual Humans in Virtual Environments for Social Training.
the perception of animated characters displaying emotional body language and the implications this has on the design of Virtual Environments used for social task training.
the question of how emotional body language is perceived.

the perception of the animated characters is affected by their appearance and that their emotional body language is perceived similarly to that by a human.
emotional body language is a valid way for animated characters, but not for realistic ones to display emotions.
the perception to an animated emotional body language displayed is similar to that of a real actor.

the perception of animated body language is similar to the one for real body language.
